claude.performance_metric: Inotera net loss $541M (CY2012); Micron equity-method losses $(112)M/$(189)M/$(79)M across FY2011–2013; no consolidation/control gained
claude.rationale: p4=1: the slice documents realized product/process friction over time — Micron disclosed "difficulties and delays in ramping production at Inotera" and "difficulties in transferring technology to Inotera," and recognized recurring losses on its Inotera purchase commitment across 2011–2012, showing the acquired product/supply arrangement could not be cleanly aligned with operating processes. p5=1: the slice documents a realized process/organization fracture — Micron determined it "do[es] not have the power to direct the activities of Inotera" due to governance-rights limitations requiring other parties' consent and Inotera's dependence on Nanya for financing and its ability to operate in Taiwan, and the parties had to renegotiate the entire JV/supply structure in January 2013, evidencing operations breaking against the organization/governance. t2=0: both parties continued a DRAM supply/JV value logic without documented irreconcilable value-capture conflict; t1 uncertain because the slice contains no controlling-intent archetype framing.

gemini.performance_metric: Equity in the net loss of Inotera was $(112) million in 2011, $(189) million in 2012, and $(79) million in 2013
gemini.rationale: The slice documents product/process disruption, noting 'difficulties and delays in ramping production at Inotera' and 'difficulties in transferring technology to Inotera.' There is no documented evidence of a process/organization fracture, as the lack of control was a governance limitation rather than an integration breakdown.

grok.performance_metric: continued equity-method losses; ownership ~35%; supply renegotiated 2013
grok.rationale: p4_pathway is coded 1 because the slice documents realized product/process disruption: Micron disclosed 'difficulties and delays in ramping production at Inotera' and 'difficulties in transferring technology to Inotera,' together with repeated losses recognized on the Inotera purchase commitment in 2011–2012 and sharply higher purchase costs ($641M to $1,260M by 2013). p5_pathway is coded 0 because, although Micron recorded that it lacked power to direct Inotera and the parties renegotiated JV/supply terms in January 2013, the slice does not document a realized fracture of operations against people/management/culture over time.
